ck7infinite.config.general.enabled.toolt:
Master switch: turns OFF the entire mod at once (all 4 modules), no need to go
module by module. For a module to work, BOTH are required: this switch AND
that module's own 'Enabled' toggle, further down this screen.
ck7infinite.config.general.sodium_warnin:
If enabled, the 'Use Fog Occlusion' chat notice won't show again when
joining a world with Sodium or Embeddium installed.
ck7infinite.config.general.potato_profil:
If enabled, the Potato PC profile suggestion won't show again when
joining a world on detected integrated graphics.
ck7infinite.config.ultraload.enabled.too:
Panic mode: when chunks are loading/generating heavily, temporarily turns off
everything that doesn't help them appear (AI, spawns, particles, entity render)
to free up CPU and GPU. Everything is restored once the load drops.
ck7infinite.config.ultraload.activation_:
How many chunks per second must load to trigger Ultra Load. Lower = activates
with little movement; higher = only while exploring hard.
ck7infinite.config.ultraload.safe_radius:
Around each player, the sacrifices that affect entities (freezing mobs,
freezing entities, hiding entities) do NOT apply, even if Ultra Load is active.
Avoids the scare of an enemy right next to you suddenly disappearing/freezing.
ck7infinite.config.ultraload.cooldown.to: How long it stays active after the load drops, to avoid flickering. 40 = 2 seconds.
ck7infinite.config.ultraload.freeze_all_:
Freezes the AI of ALL mobs (regardless of distance/vision) while loading.
Requires the Mob AI Freeze module to be enabled. Frees up the most CPU.
ck7infinite.config.ultraload.pause_spawn: Cancels natural mob spawns while loading.
ck7infinite.config.ultraload.pause_rando:
Pauses crop/grass/leaf growth, fire, ice (randomTickSpeed=0) and restores it
afterward. Also restored when disabled or when closing the world.
ck7infinite.config.ultraload.hide_partic: Discards all particles while loading (frees up CPU and GPU).
ck7infinite.config.ultraload.hide_entiti:
Doesn't render mobs/other players while loading (frees up GPU for the terrain).
They reappear once it's done.
ck7infinite.config.ultraload.freeze_enti:
AGGRESSIVE. Fully freezes entity ticking (movement/physics, not just AI) while
loading, like pausing. Frees up a lot more CPU. Doesn't affect the player or
whatever you're riding.
ck7infinite.config.ultraload.freeze_bloc:
AGGRESSIVE. Pauses hoppers/furnaces/spawners while loading. Harmless during
short bursts; if you have timing-sensitive farms and notice hiccups, set to false.
ck7infinite.config.ultraload.tier3: --- Tier 3: experimental, touches redstone/fluids and video options ---
ck7infinite.config.ultraload.pause_sched:
Pauses redstone and water/lava flow while loading (different from random
ticks). Nothing is lost, pending ticks stay queued. Real cost: redstone
clocks/pistons stop and water/lava don't flow during the burst.
ck7infinite.config.ultraload.reduce_enti:
Lowers Options.entityDistanceScaling (how far entities are drawn) while
loading. Verified to have no rebuild cost, unlike render distance.
ck7infinite.config.ultraload.entity_dist:
Multiplier to use while loading. Never raises your real value, only trims it.
Only applies if 'Reduce entity distance' is enabled.
ck7infinite.config.ultraload.limit_frame:
Counterintuitive but real on low-core-count CPUs: every frame the render
thread does NOT draw is free CPU for the chunk generation/meshing threads.
ck7infinite.config.ultraload.framerate_l:
FPS to use while loading. Never raises your real limit, only trims it. Only
applies if 'Limit FPS during load' is enabled.
ck7infinite.config.mobfreeze.enabled.too: Freezes the AI (pathfinding/goals) of mobs far from the player.
ck7infinite.config.mobfreeze.freeze_radi: Within this radius mobs keep their AI active; outside, they freeze.
ck7infinite.config.mobfreeze.require_los:
In addition to distance, freezes mobs occluded by blocks (e.g. in caves
beneath you) until there's direct line of sight. This is occlusion, it doesn't
matter where you're looking.
ck7infinite.config.mobfreeze.always_acti:
Within this radius mobs stay ALWAYS active, even without line of sight.
Cushions the check (a zombie banging on your door keeps working).
ck7infinite.config.mobfreeze.eval_interv: How many ticks between re-evaluating each mob. Higher = less CPU, slower reaction.
ck7infinite.config.mobfreeze.spawn_grace:
Time after spawning before a mob becomes eligible for freezing. Avoids
freezing them stacked up right after birth (they die more easily from entity
cramming).
ck7infinite.config.mobfreeze.ai_lod_enab:
For active (non-frozen) mobs beyond aiLodCloseRadiusBlocks, reduces how
often goal re-evaluation runs (same mechanism vanilla already uses to
stagger AI cost, just more aggressive). Movement, pathfinding and
look are never skipped -only goal re-evaluation.
ck7infinite.config.mobfreeze.ai_lod_clos:
Radius around each player where active mobs keep vanilla's full AI
rate. Beyond this (and up to freezeRadiusBlocks) aiLodDivisor applies.
ck7infinite.config.mobfreeze.ai_lod_divi:
How many ticks between goal re-evaluations for a mob in the medium
band. Vanilla uses 2; higher values re-evaluate less often. Only
applies if aiLodEnabled=true.
ck7infinite.config.mobfreeze.require_hos:
If enabled, only manages hostiles. Disabled (default) also freezes passives
(sheep, chickens, pigs), which cost ~2x what hostiles do.
ck7infinite.config.mobfreeze.type_whitel: If NOT empty, ONLY these types are eligible. E.g: minecraft:zombie
ck7infinite.config.mobfreeze.type_blackl:
Types that are NEVER frozen. Villagers are handled separately (Villager
Throttling).
ck7infinite.config.mobfreeze.modid_white: If NOT empty, ONLY mobs from these mods are eligible. E.g: minecraft, alexsmobs
ck7infinite.config.mobfreeze.modid_black: Mods whose mobs are never frozen (useful for mods with their own AI).
ck7infinite.config.villagerthrottle.enab: Freezes the AI of villagers far from the player (designed for villager halls).
ck7infinite.config.villagerthrottle.radi: Within this radius villagers keep AI active; outside, they freeze.
ck7infinite.config.villagerthrottle.eval: How many ticks between re-evaluating each villager. Higher = less CPU.
ck7infinite.config.villagerthrottle.incl: If enabled, also manages wandering traders.
ck7infinite.config.villagerthrottle.unfr:
A villager unfreezes instantly when you right-click it, even if still outside
the radius, so trading/restocking respond without delay.
ck7infinite.config.particlepriority.enab:
Prioritizes which particles to render by relevance (combat, interaction)
instead of vanilla's raw distance filter.
ck7infinite.config.particlepriority.comb: Within this radius combat particles are always shown.
ck7infinite.config.particlepriority.inte: Within this radius interaction/crafting particles are always shown.
ck7infinite.config.particlepriority.reds: Within this radius redstone particles are always shown.
ck7infinite.config.particlepriority.ambi:
Within this radius ambient particles (rain, dripping, spores) are shown at
full rate; beyond it they're discarded except for exceptions.

Very close to the player, ambient particles are shown even outside the view
cone (avoids something right at the camera disappearing).
ck7infinite.config.particlepriority.view:
0.0 = 180 degree cone (the entire front). Higher narrows the cone; negative
widens it.
ck7infinite.config.particlepriority.cont:
Radius around your last action (breaking/placing/attacking) where particles
are treated as maximum priority.
How many ticks after an action the context bonus keeps applying.
ck7infinite.config.particlepriority.ambi: Cap ambient particles by screen coverage

Caps ambient particles by estimated screen coverage (not raw count): a
particle very close to the camera costs more against the budget than
a distant one. Only affects ambient particles not tied to your last
action.

Per-frame budget, in units of 'particles equivalent to one at
ambientCloseRadiusBlocks distance' (~1.0 each). Closer particles cost
more (up to 4x), farther ones cost less. Only applies if the toggle
above is enabled.
ck7infinite.config.particlepriority.comb: IDs (path, no namespace) classified as combat.
ck7infinite.config.particlepriority.inte: IDs (path, no namespace) classified as interaction/crafting.
ck7infinite.config.particlepriority.reds: IDs (path, no namespace) classified as redstone.
ck7infinite.config.resscale.enabled.tool:
Renders the 3D world at a reduced resolution and stretches it to full screen.
Default off: new module, only enable it after trying it with your real setup.
ck7infinite.config.resscale.scale.toolti:
1.0 = native resolution (no effect). Below 1.0 = more pixelated, better
performance. Above 1.0 = sharper (supersampling), worse performance.
Applies instantly on save, no need to restart or rejoin the world.
ck7infinite.config.resscale.linear_filte:
Enabled = smooth (light FXAA-like). Disabled = nearest neighbor
(sharper/pixelated).
ck7infinite.config.resscale.aggressive_m:
Forces coarser mip levels to reduce texture bandwidth, trading some
sharpness at mid/long distance for performance. Unlike the render
scale, this applies even at scale 1.0.

How strong the forced mip bias is. Higher = more bandwidth saved,
blurrier textures at mid distance. Only applies if aggressive
mipmapping is enabled.
ck7infinite.config.resscale.renderscale_:
If enabled, the chat warning about a conflict with the RenderScale
mod won't be shown again when entering a world.
ck7infinite.resscale.renderscale_conflic: [Ck7 - Conatus] Detected the RenderScale mod installed alongside Escala de Resolucion: both swap the render target on their own, without coordinating, so having both active at once with a scale other than 1.0 breaks the frame. ck7infinite.config.simdistance.enabled.t:
Enables the module. Default false: a previous attempt at this mechanism
backfired in a real pack by not distinguishing world generation from
real simulation load. Test in your setup before enabling.
ck7infinite.config.simdistance.min_simul:
Floor for simulation distance under sustained load. The ceiling is
always your configured server/world value.
ck7infinite.config.simdistance.high_tick:
If the MEDIAN tick time over the last ~100 ticks (5s) exceeds this,
simulation distance drops by one chunk per evaluation.
ck7infinite.config.simdistance.low_tick_:
If the median tick time drops below this, simulation distance grows
by one chunk per evaluation (up to the ceiling), once the cooldown
has passed. The gap between this and the high threshold is a dead
zone that prevents oscillation.
ck7infinite.config.simdistance.eval_inte:
How often to re-evaluate and move simulation distance by at most one
chunk.
ck7infinite.config.simdistance.growth_co:
Ticks to wait after a cut before simulation distance is allowed to
grow again. Breaks the cut->unload->grow->regenerate->cut cycle that
causes oscillation.
